anomaly_def.Name: Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly + Operating System Resource Limit Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Composite Definition: The database host simultaneously suffers from storage-subsystem saturation (throughput, IOPS, or latency limits reached on underlying volumes) and exhaustion of kernel-enforced process or memory-mapping resources (file descriptors, shared-memory segments, threads, AIO contexts, etc.), creating a compounded bottleneck that is external to the database engine’s own configuration knobs.

Combined Observable Phenomena: End-to-end response times and batch windows extend unpredictably as physical read/write latency spikes coincide with intermittent engine errors such as "cannot allocate shared memory", "unable to open file", or "failed to spawn worker". Wait-class statistics show heavy data-file, log-file, and durability flush waits alongside sudden surges of metadata, latch, or connection-management waits caused by stalled background workers. CPU utilisation may appear moderate but with rising run-queue lengths when threads block on both I/O completion and kernel resource acquisition. System logs reveal kernel I/O queue overruns, IOPS throttling, plus EMFILE/ENFILE or ENOMEM errors. The overlap can lead to partial or rolling outages: long-running sessions persist yet new connections, parallel workers, or checkpoint helpers fail to start, while I/O queues deepen and checkpoint completion timeouts threaten crash recovery windows.

Causal Interaction: Sustained storage saturation elongates I/O completion times, causing a buildup of database processes and background tasks waiting on disk; this increases concurrent open files, AIO requests, semaphore consumption, and thread count, pushing the system toward its kernel resource limits. Conversely, once file-handle, AIO, or memory-mapping limits are reached, the database engine may be forced to retry or serialize I/O operations, further inflating I/O queues and intensifying storage latency. The feedback loop between physical device overload and kernel resource exhaustion thus amplifies contention at both layers, degrading throughput, starving new work, and complicating diagnosis because symptoms from each layer mask or mimic the other.

entry.error_class: Class HV - Foreign Data Wrapper Error (SQL/MED)
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
